claims.claim: Apple designs, manufactures and markets smartphones, personal computers, tablets, wearables, accessories and a variety of related services.
claims.quote: The Company designs, manufactures and markets smartphones, personal computers, tablets, wearables and accessories, and sells a variety of related services.

claims.claim: Apple’s product portfolio includes iPhone, Mac, iPad, Apple Watch, AirPods, Beats, Apple Vision Pro and a suite of software platforms (iOS, iPadOS, macOS, watchOS, visionOS, tvOS).
claims.quote: Wearables includes smartwatches, wireless headphones and spatial computers. The Company’s line of smartwatches... The Company’s line of wireless headphones includes AirPods®, AirPods Pro®, AirPods Max® and Beats® products. Apple Vision Pro® is the Company’s spatial computer based on its visionOS® operating system.

claims.claim: Apple offers fee‑based support (AppleCare®), cloud services, an app distribution platform (App Store®), subscription content services, and payment services (Apple Card®, Apple Pay®).
claims.quote: The Company offers a portfolio of fee‑based service and support products under the AppleCare® brand.

claims.claim: Apple segments its business geographically (Americas, Europe, Greater China, Japan, Rest of Asia Pacific) and serves consumer, SMB, education, enterprise and government markets through direct and indirect channels.
claims.quote: The Company manages its business primarily on a geographic basis. The Company’s reportable segments consist of the Americas, Europe, Greater China, Japan and Rest of Asia Pacific… The Company’s customers are primarily in the consumer, small and mid‑sized business, education, enterprise and government markets.

claims.claim: Apple recorded total net sales of $114.5 billion in Q4 2026, up 12 percent YoY, reflecting strong demand for iPhone and Services.
claims.quote: Apple® today announced financial results for its fiscal 2026 fourth quarter ended September 26, 2026. The Company posted quarterly revenue of $114.5 billion, up 12 percent year over year.

claims.claim: iPhone net sales reached $57.6 billion for the quarter, the largest product‑category contribution.
Apple’s installed base of active devices hit an all‑time high across all major product categories during FY 2026.
claims.quote: Thanks to our very high levels of customer satisfaction and loyalty, our installed base of active devices reached a new all‑time high across all major product categories and geographic segments.

claims.claim: Apple acknowledges intense price competition, rapid product cycles and aggressive pricing by rivals, which pressurize gross margins.
claims.quote: The markets for the Company’s products and services are highly competitive and are characterized by aggressive price competition, downward pressure on gross margins...

claims.claim: Apple holds a minority market share in the global smartphone, PC, tablet and wearables markets, making it vulnerable to competitors’ pricing tactics.
claims.quote: The Company has a minority market share in the global smartphone, personal computer, tablet and wearables markets...

claims.claim: Supply constraints for advanced semiconductors, memory and storage are expected to intensify, potentially limiting component availability and raising costs.
claims.quote: the Company is experiencing supply constraints and rising costs driven by industry‑wide supply‑demand imbalances for key components, including advanced semiconductors, memory and storage. These constraints ... The Company expects these trends to intensify for memory and storage components.

claims.claim: Management indicates continued investment in artificial‑intelligence features, infrastructure and new hardware (e.g., “iPhone Duo” and “all‑new Siri AI”).
claims.quote: ... we’re closing the year with our most ambitious lineup yet. That includes the iPhone Duo, the most transformational iPhone since the original, alongside iPhone 18 Pro... We also just introduced a whole new generation of hardware for the home and brought Touch to Mac for the first time. Together with the all‑new Siri AI...

claims.claim: Apple plans to expand its data‑center capacity to support AI and cloud services, but acknowledges the large capital outlays, long‑term commitments and external constraints (e.g., power, water, zoning).
claims.quote: Investment in data center capacity involves significant expenditures and long‑term commitments, including for components and equipment, which increase the Company’s capital expenditures, liabilities and obligations...

claims.claim: Apple faces regulatory risk from the EU Digital Markets Act (DMA) that may force interoperability and limit certain revenue streams.
claims.quote: The DMA imposes interoperability obligations on the Company requiring it to make certain of its technologies and features available to third‑party products and services for free, which increases security and privacy risks, requires significant engineering resources, and can adversely affect the functionality, competitiveness, and user experience of the Company’s products.

claims.claim: Judgment: Apple should diversify its semiconductor and memory supplier base to mitigate the supply‑constraint risk highlighted in its 10‑K.
claims.quote: The Company also competes for various components ... many components used by the Company, including those that are available from multiple sources, are at times subject to industry‑wide shortages and significant commodity pricing fluctuations.

claims.claim: Judgment: Accelerating development of proprietary AI chips could reduce reliance on third‑party compute capacity and lower long‑term operating costs.
claims.quote: The Company competes with a number of companies in the development and deployment of artificial intelligence and has made significant investments in building artificial intelligence features and related infrastructure across its products and services.

gaps: The 10‑K excerpt does not provide quantitative forecasts for FY 2027 revenue, product launch timing, or specific market‑share targets, so forward‑looking growth numbers cannot be cited.
No explicit management guidance on new product pricing, channel strategy, or planned share‑repurchase volumes beyond the Q4 dividend is present in the supplied text.
insight: Insight: Apple reported iPhone achieving a September quarter record and Services reaching an all‑time high — EX-99.1 line 13: "Today, Apple is proud to report a September quarter revenue record of $114.5 billion, up 12 percent from a year ago, with iPhone reaching a September quarter record and Services reaching an all‑time high, capping off our best fiscal year ever,"
